resolved_findings.change: Initial erase C5 becomes ClearRejectedError; errors during polls and completion readback become ClearAcceptedError. execute retains owner and outcome-unknown for accepted intent and only treats initial explicit rejection as no effect.
resolved_findings.independent_evidence: Initial C5 => failed/unowned. Accepted erase followed by poll C5 or info-readback C5 => outcome-unknown/owned, archive survives a 400-day future cleanup cutoff.

resolved_findings.change: Device fingerprint network proof precedes a rollback/fresh BEGIN IMMEDIATE authority transaction. Server lifecycle, stable binding, revisions, owner, consent and current credential pair are checked before the conditional dispatch-intent transition commits. Non-SQLite dispatch fails closed.
resolved_findings.independent_evidence: 12 real-route cases: each enable/clear/clock final fingerprint interleaved with committed lifecycle, policy revision, binding/protocol, or credential revocation => failed and zero mutation commands. Existing narrow concurrent transition test independently rerun: revocation writer serializes behind accepted intent.
resolved_findings.acceptance_boundary: Durable serialized dispatch-intent commit defines acceptance. A later revocation cannot guarantee cancellation between that commit and the BMC write; no claim of hardware-atomic revocation is made.

resolved_findings.change: Fingerprint records complete Get Device ID bytes, explicit auxiliary-field presence/value and identity capability; adapter version advances to sel-raw-v2. Qualification requires a matching firmware_identity_scope and exact fingerprint.
resolved_findings.independent_evidence: Two distinct auxiliary revisions and absent auxiliary bytes yield three distinct identities; changes revoke both automatic consents. Altered auxiliary firmware fails existing synthetic qualification.
resolved_findings.limit: The trusted operator must still establish that the chosen device identity capability distinguishes the exact firmware under qualification; generic Get Device ID values are not a substitute for vendor-specific firmware acceptance evidence.
